title: Which finding would weaken or challenge the claim
subtitle: Command of Evidence · 6 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **6 of the official questions in Command of Evidence are this one** — 0 Easy, 2 Medium, 4 Hard.
It is top-heavy: most versions are Hard, so it only earns study time once your target actually requires that tier.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:

- The question stem uses 'weaken', 'undermine', 'challenge' or 'call into question', or it asks for support for someone who argues against an earlier view, such as a team disputing other experts' interpretation.
- You have to notice the direction of the question before anything else.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Circle the direction word in the stem, and identify which claim is being attacked and whose side you are on.
- 2) State what would have to be true for that claim to hold.
- 3) Choose the choice that removes that condition or offers a better alternative explanation for the evidence.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You answer the opposite question and pick the choice that strengthens the claim, because it is the one that feels most connected to the passage.
In rebuttal passages, you back the experts being rebutted instead of the researchers doing the rebutting.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
You answer the opposite question and pick the choice that strengthens the claim, because it is the one that feels most connected to the passage.
In rebuttal passages, you back the experts being rebutted instead of the researchers doing the rebutting.
